summary: Naming remains a product decision for Robert. Companion App is the recommendation because it is concrete, non-academic and accommodates both the minimal HTML form and a richer interactive product.

items.text: Companion App — recommended. Tangible and product-ready; broad enough for a generated site, interactive wiki, graph or canvas. Its generic wording needs a strong one-line definition.
Comprehension Layer — accurate and broad, but sounds architectural and academic rather than like something a developer would open and use.
Cognitive Sidecar — memorable and structurally apt, but both words are technical; sidecar also collides with the narrower sidecar-metadata pattern.
Catch-up Companion — makes the speed gap immediately clear, but sounds remedial and temporary although ongoing system care is equally important.
System Companion — plain and product-capable, but too generic and easily confused with companion-model.
Comprehension Companion — precise and distinctive, but less natural in speech and slightly more academic than Companion App.
The wiki-shaped implementation is already captured by wiki-as-cognitive-interface; reuse its layered content model.
Use predictable companion files for provenance, fingerprints, ownership and review state.
Generate and cache artifact-specific views when a fixed renderer cannot provide the needed task surface.
Keep the companion synchronized in both directions instead of assuming generation alone prevents drift.
